records.Concise description: A widely used open-source Bitcoin wallet emphasizing simple mobile self-custody while retaining multisig, PSBT, coin-control and advanced transaction tools.
records.Deeper researched summary: BlueWallet keeps on-chain Bitcoin keys on the user's device and supports single-signature, watch-only and multisig wallets, hardware signing, PSBTs, coin control, RBF/CPFP and PayJoin. Its historical hosted Lightning service was sunset in 2023; Lightning functionality should now be described in terms of user-connected/self-hosted LNDHub or other current integrations rather than the former BlueWallet-hosted account service.
records.Launch / history: BlueWallet emerged in 2017 and remains actively maintained; version 8.x releases shipped in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: BlueWallet helped combine approachable mobile Bitcoin self-custody with power-user features such as multisig, watch-only accounts and hardware-wallet coordination.
Important technical or cultural characte: iOS and Android; desktop support through current project clients where offered
records.Verification basis: Current first-party features and 2026 releases verify active maintenance; LNDHub source material is used to separate current connection support from the retired hosted Lightning service.
Research notes / uncertainties: BlueWallet's former hosted Lightning/LndHub service was sunset in 2023; do not publish 'BlueWallet Lightning is self-custodial' without specifying the user's backend arrangement.
On-chain self-custody and Lightning account custody are separate questions.

records.Concise description: Blockstream's open-source self-custody app for Bitcoin and Liquid, evolved from Blockstream Green and integrating the Jade hardware-wallet family.
records.Deeper researched summary: Blockstream App is the successor branding to Blockstream Green. It supports Bitcoin and Liquid across mobile and desktop, can connect to a user's own Bitcoin node, supports Tor-oriented privacy options and integrates deeply with Blockstream Jade. In 2025–2026 it added Lightning payment flows using swap-based interoperability; Blockstream was still working toward a more vertically integrated native Lightning experience in 2026, so 'Lightning support' must be qualified by implementation.
Creators / founders: Lawrence Nahum — GreenAddress founder; GreenAddress lineage later acquired by Blockstream
records.Launch / history: GreenAddress predates Blockstream's ownership; Blockstream Green became Blockstream App in May 2025. The app remained actively developed through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is a major bridge between ordinary Bitcoin self-custody, Liquid, hardware signing and Blockstream's broader wallet stack.
Important technical or cultural characte: Lightning payment interoperability through swaps in current releases

Official sources.label: Blockstream Green to Blockstream App announcement

records.Verification basis: Current Blockstream product pages and 2025–2026 first-party release material verify rebrand, platform support, wallet custody model and evolving Lightning integration.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply current Lightning functionality is necessarily a native Lightning-node wallet; current product flows have included Liquid/Lightning swaps while native Lightning work continues.
Treat GreenAddress and Blockstream Green as product history, not separate canonical profiles.

records.Concise description: Andreas Schildbach's long-running standalone Android Bitcoin wallet, historically notable for direct peer-to-peer operation without a centralized wallet backend.
records.Deeper researched summary: The open-source Bitcoin Wallet for Android is one of the earliest mobile Bitcoin wallets. It stores keys locally and was designed to communicate with the Bitcoin network without a centralized custodial backend. It remains downloadable/cataloged, but current August 2026 maintainer activity could not be verified strongly enough from first-party release evidence to classify the project ACTIVE.
records.Launch / history: First released in 2011. The official repository shows meaningful historical development, but the research pass did not verify a substantive 2026 release or maintainer activity statement.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is historically important as an early native Android Bitcoin wallet and a reference point for non-custodial mobile Bitcoin use.
Important technical or cultural characte: Peer-to-peer / lightweight chain synchronization rather than a custodial backend
records.Verification basis: Official repository verifies identity and architecture; current catalog availability corroborates usability, but no sufficiently current first-party lifecycle evidence was found for August 2026.
Research notes / uncertainties: Lifecycle remains UNCERTAIN: downloadability and a listing do not prove active 2026 maintenance.
Do not present stale feature claims as current without a fresh release-level check.

records.Concise description: An open-source desktop Bitcoin wallet focused on network privacy, coin control and WabiSabi CoinJoin coordination.
records.Deeper researched summary: Wasabi is a non-custodial Bitcoin desktop wallet centered on privacy. The zkSNACKs-operated default CoinJoin coordinator shut down in June 2024, but the wallet project continued. Current Wasabi versions allow users to configure third-party WabiSabi coordinators and include privacy-oriented networking, coin selection and PayJoin support. Since version 2.8-era changes, chain-filter acquisition also moved away from the former Wasabi backend toward peer-to-peer mechanisms.
records.Launch / history: Wasabi launched in 2018. The default zkSNACKs CoinJoin coordinator stopped operating June 1, 2024; the wallet continued as actively maintained open-source software through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Wasabi is one of the most influential Bitcoin privacy wallets and popularized WabiSabi-based CoinJoin coordination and privacy-oriented desktop wallet UX.
Important technical or cultural characte: WabiSabi CoinJoin client with user-selected coordinator
No default zkSNACKs CoinJoin coordinator after June 2024
records.Verification basis: Current official wallet/docs/repository plus project history verify continued software development and the post-2024 coordinator model.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply zkSNACKs still provides the default CoinJoin coordinator.
A CoinJoin coordinator participates in coordination but, by protocol design, is not a custodian of wallet keys; this does not eliminate all privacy or implementation risks.
